summary: Round 7, prose only: no production logic, no wire change, and no object-store request added, moved or authorised by this diff. I did what was asked and attacked the DECISIONS rather than the sentences, and I re-verified each of them against source rather than against the fix text. (a) holds and its four counted facts are true in the tree: MemoryBinStore.java:266 and LocalFsBinStore.java:434 both pass `false` for presign; every `implements SubscriptionTransport` in the tree is in a test source set (client/src/test, plugin/src/test, plugin/src/clusterTest) so production implementations really are 0; check-io-seam.sh:58 excludes exactly one module; client/build.gradle.kts declares exactly `api(project(":format"))`; and check-module.sh:234/236 carry the NO_HTTP and NO_CLOUD lists the record quotes. (b) holds on the only ground it now claims: SegmentWriter.java:98 sets byteStart to PREAMBLE_BYTES + headerLen and advances it per block, so the wire copy is an ABSOLUTE object offset and the slice GET really can be issued at event-receipt time; the arithmetic re-derives independently (7/129 = 5.43%, 11,200/206,400 = 5.43%, 11,200/8,388,608 = 0.1335%, 206,400/8,388,608 = 2.46%, cross-check 0.1335/2.46 = 5.43% and 40.4x, measured 6/128 = 4.69%). I ALSO CHECKED THE PREDICTION AGAINST THE COST MODEL AS ASKED, AND IT IS RIGHT -- more strongly than the record claims. docs/research/00-problem/02-cost-model.md:29 states it as a primary fact ('Bytes moved between S3 and same-region compute are free. Only requests cost money'), R4:287 turns it into a design rule ('wasted same-region bytes are free, extra requests are not'), R7 prefers one speculative range read over a read-footer-then-read-index two-step, and docs/research/30-design-space/05-az-topology-and-data-flow.md:58 says OpenSearch nodes read from the object store 'free, in-region'. So a two-request bounded read against the store is strictly worse on the only currency cost.md governs, at every K, and 'expect removal to be right' is the correct prediction. I independently swept the tree for the seven patterns and every file that matches byteStart/byteLen is in the sweep table (including backlog.md, added this round); the other pattern hits outside the table -- SubscriptionHub.java:494, SegmentProxy.java:387, SegmentPublisher.java:146, Grant.java:7, BinStoreOffset.java:20 -- are all a different sense and none asserts a retired claim. WHAT BLOCKS IS THE ROUND-6 FIX ITSELF, HALF-LANDED: ADR-0044:122 ends the new tie-break paragraph with 'M5.66 carries the assertion', and the M5.66 cell added by this same commit (backlog.md:126) contains no such criterion -- no mention of the two copies disagreeing, of the directory being authoritative, or of refusing rather than decoding. That is the exact mechanism this record's own Decision (c) documents at :168-175 as how ADR-0043 lost security.md rule 3's range half to M5.45b: a clause handed to a row whose numbered criteria do not mention it, after which the row takes an arm, discharges the criteria it has, and marks itself done.

findings.title: ADR-0044 says 'M5.66 carries the assertion' for the directory-wins tie-break; the M5.66 cell written by the same commit carries no such criterion
findings.summary: :114-123 is new this round and states a correctness rule: the event's coordinates are a HINT that buys concurrency, the segment's directory is the truth, and 'a bounded reader that finds them disagreeing must refuse rather than decode', because otherwise 'the consumer has fetched the wrong bytes under a valid signature, which is ADR-0032's silent data error one layer out'. The paragraph closes 'M5.66 carries the assertion.' It does not. backlog.md:126 (M5.66, added by this commit) has four numbered criteria: (1) the measured crossover recorded in ADR-0044, (2) the bounded reader with the codec acted on, bytes and requests counted at two shares plus the slice-before-header RTT clause, (3) the sweep table corrected or re-confirmed, (4) security.md rule 3's range half. Grepping that cell for 'disagree', 'tie-break', 'hint', 'truth', 'authoritative', 'mismatch' and 'agree' returns nothing; its only two `RunEntry` mentions are the possibility refutation and the codec fixture. Criterion 2 requires 'a consumer that uses the EVENT's coordinates to drive it' and requires the slice request be issued before the header response is delivered -- i.e. it mandates the parallel design and says nothing about validating it. The tie-break is also not a row of the sweep table, which criterion 3 is pointed at as THE enumeration, so no later sweep reaches it either. This is the same shape as round 6's two majors, reproduced inside the fix for round 6's minor.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's owner takes criterion 2's first arm. They fetch [0, PREAMBLE + headerLen) and, concurrently, [event.byteStart(), event.byteStart() + event.byteLen()) -- which criterion 2 now REQUIRES to be issued before the header response arrives. They assert two requests at K = 1, crossover and crossover + 1, assert bytes bounded above, assert the codec flag is read from the fetched directory and refused, record the crossover in ADR-0044, correct every sweep-table row, answer security.md rule 3, and mark the row done. Every criterion is green and no case anywhere compares the event's extent with the RunEntry the same reader has just fetched. A publisher off-by-one, a v3 event replayed against a rewritten object, or a run index skew then decodes a slice taken from the wrong offset: either a throw inside the record loop or -- the case that matters -- records from the neighbouring run handed to the shard with the offset advancing, under a signature that validates, which is precisely the silent data error :118-119 names ADR-0032 for. The rule exists only in a record whose own Decision (c) says a clause handed to a row that does not number it is closed by nobody.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the clause to backlog.md:126 as part of criterion 2's first arm, in one sentence, so it has an assertion form: 'AND THE EVENT'S EXTENT IS CHECKED AGAINST THE DIRECTORY'S AND A DISAGREEMENT REFUSES -- ADR-0044 makes the event a HINT and the directory the TRUTH, and the parallel design is the only one where two copies are in play; asserted by patching a RunEntry byteStart/byteLen to disagree with the event (the same GoldenSegmentV1Test technique the codec fixture uses -- patch the directory entry, recompute the header CRC) and requiring the reader to throw rather than decode, because the natural implementation decodes the slice it already holds.' ADR-0044:122 can then stay as written. Alternatively, if this is judged M5.45h's or a new row's, change :122 to name the row that actually has it.

findings.title: The prediction's escape clause names a price no path in this architecture pays: an object-store GET is never billed cross-AZ, and cross-AZ peer transfer is designed out
findings.summary: The prediction at :140-149 is correct on its main claim and I verified it independently -- cost-model:29 ('Bytes moved between S3 and same-region compute are free. Only requests cost money'), R4:287, R7, and doc 05:58 ('read segment byte ranges directly from the object store -- free, in-region') all say the two-request bounded read loses on dollars at every K. What is loose is the escape clause: 'removing them is right unless the cross-AZ case or a latency budget says otherwise'. R12's $0.02/GB is EC2 cross-AZ transfer (ADR-0012, the peer mesh), and it is not reachable on the path being priced: the bounded read's +1 request is an object-store GET, whose bytes are in-region and free whichever AZ the node sits in. The only path that does pay $0.02/GB is a cross-AZ peer fetch, which carries no object-store request at all -- and backlog.md:109 (M5.9) makes it 'not addressable by construction', citing ADR-0012's 419x measurement, with `Membership` declaring no method that takes an AZ. So the record names two conditions and one of them cannot occur. backlog.md:126 inherits the same menu -- 'cross-AZ dollars at R12's rate, or TIME'.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's owner reads criterion 1's instruction to name the price model first, sees the record and the row both offer 'cross-AZ dollars at R12's rate' as a live quantity, and prices the bounded read with it: one saved GET's worth is 19.5 KiB, while the bounded path avoids ~8 MiB, so the bounded read wins by roughly 400x at every K. They record that crossover IN ADR-0044, as criterion 1 requires, and keep the fields on it -- a number derived from a transfer price that no request on the direct path incurs, written into the one record the ADR declares the single place the number is derived. The correct in-region answer, which the very same paragraph states, is a crossover of 0 and the removal arm.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not open a round 8 for this -- rule 11. Record it in the commit body, or tighten the clause to 'unless a latency budget says otherwise' with one half-sentence saying why cross-AZ is not the other half: R12's rate applies to peer transfer, which M5.9 makes unaddressable, and never to the object-store GET the bounded read adds.
